objectives: Identify and remediate short /o/ weaknesses revealed by the diagnostic.
Use minimal contrasts to repair /o/ versus /a/ confusion.
Strengthen decoding, encoding, comprehension or fluency according to the diagnosed gap.
Reassess with fresh items and make an evidence-based advance-or-reteach decision.
concepts: Remediation should target the diagnosed component.
Minimal contrasts make vowel differences explicit.
Progression depends on evidence rather than completion speed.

definitions.definition: Instruction focused on a specific diagnosed learning gap.
A follow-up check using new items to determine whether the target skill improved.
An evidence-based decision to advance or provide further reteaching.

workedExamples: hot/hat → compare middle phonemes → map o/a → read and spell both.
dog/dag → isolate the middle vowel → decode again.
Accurate but slow → repeated accurate reading before increasing speed.
commonMistakes: Reteaching everything instead of the diagnosed gap.
Advancing because a learner finished quickly.
Increasing speed before accuracy is secure.
keyTakeaways: Advance only when evidence supports it.
revisionPoints: Diagnose → target → practise → reassess → advance or reteach.

conceptual: Identify the component skill behind an error.
application: Repair decoding and spelling errors with sound-to-letter mapping.
higherOrderThinking: Choose the appropriate instructional decision from diagnostic evidence.
mixedReview: Combine vowel contrast, decoding, spelling, comprehension and fluency repair.

formulaOrFactBank: Mastery decision = evidence against a defined target
mistakeBasedRevision: o/a confusion → auditory contrast + grapheme mapping.
slow accurate reading → repeated accurate rereading.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat only the weak component, then use fresh reassessment items.

outcomes: Learner improves the diagnosed short /o/ component with targeted practice.
Learner distinguishes short /o/ from /a/ in taught contrasts with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner applies corrected sound-spelling mapping to new CVC items.
Teacher can make an evidence-based advance-or-reteach decision.

questions.question: If a learner confuses hot and hat, what should be practised?
Which middle sound is in hot?
Which spelling completes h _ t for “hot”?
If dog is read as dag, what should the learner compare?
If pot is written as pat, which part is incorrect?
What is the best first response when a learner guesses a familiar word-family word?
Which pair is useful for short /o/ versus short /a/ contrast practice?
After targeted practice, what should happen next?
options: Reassess the same skill with new items

questions.question: A learner reads accurately but slowly. What is the priority?
A learner decodes accurately but misses sentence questions. What needs support?
What result supports advancing to the next phonics pattern?
options: The learner meets the defined accuracy target across required component skills

questions.question: If the accuracy target is not met, what should happen?
options: Reteach the specific weak skill and reassess again

questions.question: What is the main goal of this lesson?
options: Repair short /o/ errors and verify readiness before progression
